summary: Butts County tower on a Georgia list (740 ft) and a topo-map site; the Eastern page's Pisgah National Forest label conflicts with geography; no history found.

evidence.supports: Georgia list places a Butts Lookout Tower in Butts County at 33.293 N, 84.009 W, 740 ft
Topo-map site lists the tower in the towers category for Butts County
evidence.quote: Butts Lookout Tower is listed in the Towers Category for Butts County in the state of Georgia.

evidence.supports: Topo-map site gives an approximate elevation of 741 ft (226 m)
Eastern US Lookouts Butts Mountain page gives Butts County and Pisgah National Forest
Pisgah National Forest lies entirely within North Carolina
evidence.quote: The Pisgah National Forest is completely contained within the state of North Carolina.

evidence.supports: NHLR Georgia index lists 29 registered lookouts, none named Butts
evidence.quote: There are 29 lookouts registered in Georgia.

corrections.why: Pisgah National Forest lies wholly within North Carolina, so it cannot administer a Georgia tower; no Georgia agency source was found

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Georgia list gives 740 ft and the topo-map site 741 ft; both round to 226 m, so the story gives both figures

sources.title: Butts Lookout Tower Topo Map in Butts County GA

notes_for_editor: The brief's agency, Pisgah National Forest, comes from the Eastern US Lookouts page and conflicts with geography; the correction proposes dropping it, but no Georgia agency source was found. Elevation is 740 ft on the list and 741 ft on TopoZone. A second Butts County row, butts new (GA405, 643 ft, 33.256414, -83.966601, code gfc-405?), is not explained by any source and is not in the story; an editor may want to check whether it relates to GA012. The brief's other name, butts mountain, is the title of the Eastern page. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the story now says the Eastern Butts Mountain page 'appears to cover the same site', because no source names the link between the two; the story's category wording was dropped to avoid copying the TopoZone sentence. The Georgia list prints no unit for elevation; feet is inferred from its Brasstown row (4735, which cannot be metres in Georgia) and matches TopoZone's feet figure for this tower. Confidence low.
